0.long_answer: Ionizing radiation is defined as radiation that carries enough energy to detach electrons from atoms or molecules, creating ions. This ability to ionize atoms can lead to significant cellular damage, including DNA mutations, which in turn increases the risk of developing cancers, including brain cancers. It is the only confirmed risk factor for brain tumors, and exposure to high-energy ionizing radiation (such as X-rays and gamma rays) is known to disrupt the normal cellular processes, ultimately contributing to tumor formation.
